text: You're online shopping, adding items to your cart. Distraction hits, the tab closes, and you assume your selections are gone.
Later, you revisit the store. Surprisingly, your cart is still full! Every item you picked out is waiting, exactly where you left it.
You might think it’s browser magic, or just luck. You picture your computer holding tiny digital notes, a private memory for you.
But it's the website. Using a cookie or login, it identifies you and saves your cart on its servers, linking it to your identity.
This isn't just convenience. It’s a clever system, a gentle nudge to bring you back. Your abandoned cart is an invitation to complete your purchase.
Next time you see a saved cart, you’ll understand. It’s not just a feature; it’s the invisible hand of commerce, ready to reel you back in.
